text:
Sarah: Quick Q on the chat/completions contract — I noticed ambiguity around streaming deltas and tool/function-calling fields. Specifically:
- Are partial tool calls allowed in the streaming deltas (i.e., multiple delta events that build up arguments)?
- What is the expected final shape: should the final assembled message use `function_call` (old name) or `tool_call` (new name)?

Ping @Mike for API semantics so SDKs can be updated before the rollout.

Mike: Short answer: yes, we want to support incremental tool args in stream deltas to avoid buffering large arg payloads. Design note: streaming_delta can emit repeated `tool_call` fragments with `name` and `arguments_chunk`. Final event should include `tool_call` with `arguments` fully assembled. We'll keep a compatibility layer that also emits `function_call` in the final non-stream (or final delta) for older clients.

Leo: To add: compatibility layer will add a final `function_call` object only if the client requests legacy mode via header `X-Client-Compat: function_call`. Otherwise only `tool_call` is present to avoid duplication. This keeps SDKs forward-looking but preserves old behavior.

Tina: Heads-up — the SDK codegen currently assumes `function_call` is non-null and tries to parse args as a single string. If we switch to chunking we need parsing helpers. PR #456 touches that parser. I can adapt codegen to stitch `arguments_chunk` pieces, but would like a feature flag for rollout.

Alex: Also watch the streaming field ordering. Our reassembly code in the runtime expects deltas to arrive in order, but network reorder is possible. We should add a `seq` integer on delta fragments so the SDK can reorder safely before concatenation.

Sarah: Good point about seq. Suggest we specify: `streaming_delta` fragments contain { seq: int, type: "tool_args" | "tool_name", payload: string } and final delta has `final: true` + assembled `tool_call`. That keeps proto minimal.

Mike: Agreed. I'll update the contract doc. Plan:
1) Add `seq` and `final` to streaming delta spec.
2) Final assembled event will include `tool_call` and, when legacy header set, `function_call` alias.
3) Add unit tests for reassembly + out-of-order fragments.

Tina: I can own the SDK changes + tests. Will add a feature flag `stream_tool_partial=true` behind an opt-in config in the SDK and Console rollout.

Leo: I'll update the server-side reassembly to tolerate missing fragments for 200ms then error; also emit a reassembly debug trace for troubleshooting.

Alex: For the docs and examples, here's a quick streaming sequence example — use this in the API contract doc:

```json
// stream event 1
{ "delta": { "seq": 1, "type": "tool_name", "payload": "weather.report" } }
// event 2
{ "delta": { "seq": 2, "type": "tool_args", "payload": "{\"loc\":\"NYC\",\"days\":2" } }
// event 3 (final)
{ "delta": { "seq": 3, "type": "tool_args", "payload": ",\"units\":\"metric\"", "final": true }, "tool_call": { "name": "weather.report", "arguments": "{\"loc\":\"NYC\",\"days\":2,\"units\":\"metric\"}" } }
```
Sarah: That example helps a lot. Can we also add a short note about size limits for chunking (e.g., 64KB per chunk) and content-encoding expectations?

Mike: Will add 64KB chunk size guideline and require UTF-8. Also adding a small integration test in eng-runtime to simulate reordering.

deploy-bot: CI build for PR #456 started — https://ci.redwood/456 :robot_face:

Tina: Thanks, I'll watch CI and follow up on PR comments. I'll also add the feature flag and opt-in docs in Console tickets.

Sarah: OK — next steps: Mike update contract + draft compatibility appendix; Tina implement SDK reassembly + flag; Leo add server timeout/reassembly logging; Alex validate runtime ordering assumptions. We'll sync in async and call out blockers here. :thumbsup:

Mike: I'll post the updated spec link when ready. ETA EOD PST.

Tina: ETA tomorrow morning for SDK changes.

Leo: I'll land server changes behind a feature flag by EOD as well.

Alex: I'll add a unit test to the runtime repo tonight.

Sarah: Awesome — thanks everyone. If anyone runs into major blockers, drop them here or @sarah directly.
